MCP (model context protocol) started life as a niche anthropic spec in late 2024. 
eighteen months later it's the standard plug every serious AI agent speaks — claude code, gemini cli, codex, cursor, windsurf, all of them. 
the pitch is boringly simple: instead of every model writing a custom integration for every tool, each model speaks MCP once and every tool that speaks it back becomes available. 
anthropic calls it a USB-C port for AI. that's the right mental model.
hey, I'm m0h. researcher and content creator on X, 5+ years in. I write daily content like this breaking down AI, agents, and the tools shaping the new world, in a way that actually helps you use them.   

follow + repost so others can see this, and bookmark it. you'll want to come back to it.
the catalog is now enormous. over 20,000 servers sit on public registries and the sdk was pulling ~97 million downloads a month by march 2026. 
most of them are junk, abandoned weekend projects, half-finished experiments, or worse. 
a recent audit found security issues in roughly two-thirds of the popular ones. so before anything else, three rules that matter more than this whole list:
don't install 50. more than 5-7 connected servers and your agent starts choking on tool bloat — it gets slower and dumber. pick the 3-5 that match what you actually do. this is a menu, not a shopping spree.
treat every server like a cli from a stranger's github. pin versions. scope tokens to read-only until you've watched how the agent uses them. prefer vendor-official over random forks.
never enable writes against production from an agent loop. point at a read replica or a snapshot.
one quick note on installs. the three big agents each have their own config path but the underlying json is basically identical:
claude code → claude mcp add <name> ... (or --transport http for hosted servers)
codex → codex mcp add <name> -- <command>, or edit ~/.codex/config.toml
gemini cli → edit ~/.gemini/settings.json, same mcpServers block
where a server is hosted (an https url) it usually works in all three with the http transport and a browser oauth flow. 
where it's local (npx/uvx) you drop the same command block into each agent's config. i'll give the claude command for each and note when codex/gemini differ.
let's go. grouped by what you actually do for a living.
 
the universal core — install these first
these five work everywhere and earn their slot on almost any machine.
1. github
repos, pull requests, issues, code search across your whole org — without leaving the terminal. 
pair it with sentry and your agent can read a production error and open the fixing PR in one move. 
the official server replaced all the community forks in 2026; don't use anything else.
install: 
 
 (or complete the oauth flow via /mcp after adding)
link: https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server
gotcha: scope the token. read-only unless the agent genuinely needs to push. the old @modelcontextprotocol/server-github npm package is no longer supported — use the hosted server above.
2. context7
the one that stops your agent hallucinating package APIs. instead of generating code against stale training data, it pulls current, version-pinned docs at query time. essential for fast-moving frameworks and cloud sdks.
install: 
 
codex: 
 
link: https://context7.com
gotcha: free, with an optional api key for higher rate limits.
3. playwright
a real browser the agent can drive, open pages, click, fill forms, screenshot, run smoke tests you describe in plain english. microsoft maintains it.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp
gotcha: great for exploratory testing, wrong tool for release-critical regression — you want deterministic scripts there. on windows, claude code defaults to git bash; switch it to cmd or commands fail.
4. filesystem
scoped local file access beyond the agent's working directory. stdio, local, fast.
install:  (pass the allowed paths as args)
 
link: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/filesystem
gotcha: only expose the directories you want reachable. this is a broad permission, treat it like one. (this is one of the handful of servers anthropic still actively maintains in the main reference repo.)
5. brave search
fast web search inside the agent so it can ground answers without you tab-switching.
install: (brave api key in env)
 
link: https://github.com/brave/brave-search-mcp-server
gotcha: needs a free key. keep it in user-scope settings, never commit it. note: the old @modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search reference server was archived — brave maintains its own now.
 
databases & backend
6. postgres
direct sql against your database — schema-aware debugging, data-shape checks before you write a migration.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/postgres
gotcha: heads up — anthropic's reference postgres server was archived. the npm package still installs and works, but it's unmaintained. for anything serious in 2026, use your provider's official server (supabase/neon below) or @bytebase/dbhub, which claude's own docs now point to. read-only by default. never point it at prod writes.
7. supabase
your whole backend through chat — database, auth, storage, edge functions. official, actively maintained.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/supabase-community/supabase-mcp
gotcha: start in read-only mode. it ships with that default for a reason — flip writes on only once you trust the loop.
8. neon
serverless postgres with a killer feature: branch-based migrations. when the agent runs a migration it spins up an instant copy-on-write branch off prod data, tests there, then applies. official.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/neondatabase/mcp-server-neon
gotcha: neon went all-in on the hosted remote server — the local npm package and stdio cli were removed in early 2026. use the url.
9. sqlite
local sql against a .db file. perfect for poking at datasets or debugging embedded storage.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/johnnyoshika/mcp-server-sqlite-npx
gotcha: the anthropic reference sqlite server was archived too. mcp-server-sqlite-npx is the maintained community replacement most setups use now.
10. redis
inspect keys, manage caches, monitor memory — without memorizing redis cli. official, from redis themselves.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/redis/mcp-redis
gotcha: lock it down with a redis acl read-only user before you connect an agent.
 
ops, infra & cloud
11. cloudflare
workers, dns, r2, kv, zero trust — the whole api. the main server covers 2,500+ endpoints through two tools (search/execute) using ~1k tokens instead of leaking the whole spec.
install: add 
 
to your config; connect and you're redirected to cloudflare to authorize and pick permissions
link: https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp
gotcha: cloudflare also ships product-specific servers (docs, observability, dns analytics). use the focused one if you only need a slice.
12. vercel
deploys, env vars, log inspection. official.
install: 
 
link: https://vercel.com/docs/mcp
gotcha: deploy and env-var changes are real side effects. keep a human in the loop on anything that ships.
13. aws
ec2, s3, lambda, rds via natural language.
install: aws publishes per-service MCP servers; install the ones you need from the awslabs repo
link: https://github.com/awslabs/mcp
gotcha: iam scope is everything here. give the agent a tightly-scoped role, not your admin keys.
14. docker hub
image search, tag management — useful if you live in containers.
install:
 
link: https://hub.docker.com
gotcha: community-maintained. read the source before granting it anything beyond read.
15. sentry
issues, stack traces, event detail piped straight into the agent. the github + sentry combo is the killer one — read a prod error, propose a PR.
install: 
 
link: https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/
gotcha: stack traces and breadcrumbs can carry sensitive data. mind what you're feeding the model.
16. kubernetes
cluster inspection and kubectl-style ops in plain english.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/Flux159/mcp-server-kubernetes
gotcha: community-maintained. point it at a non-prod context first. an agent with cluster write access is a bad day waiting to happen.
 
corporate / team & productivity
17. slack
messages, channel history, posting.
install: the original anthropic reference server was archived and is now maintained by zencoder as @zencoderai/slack-mcp-server (npx, with slack bot/app tokens in env). check the repo for the current token setup.
link: https://github.com/zencoderai/slack-mcp-server
gotcha: i couldn't confirm an official slack-hosted remote endpoint, so use the maintained community server rather than a guessed url. posting to channels is a side effect with an audience — confirm before the agent sends anything human-visible.
18. linear
issues, sprint planning, search. official remote server.
install: add the remote server and complete oauth; linear's docs page has the current endpoint and one-click setup for each client
link: https://linear.app/docs/mcp
gotcha: permissions inherit your linear access. the agent can do what you can do.
19. notion
pages and databases. official hosted server (makenotion), replaced the community forks.
install:  
 
then complete oauth
link: https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/mcp
gotcha: scope the integration to the workspaces you want reachable, not everything. notion is prioritizing the remote server and may sunset the local one.
20. jira / confluence (atlassian rovo)
issues, confluence docs, compass. official atlassian rovo remote server covers all of them.
install: 
 
then complete oauth
link: https://www.atlassian.com/platform/remote-mcp-server
gotcha: the older /v1/sse endpoint stops working after june 30, 2026 — use the /mcp endpoint above. oauth 2.1, respects your existing access controls.
21. google drive
file search and read across your drive.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/gdrive
gotcha: this reference server was archived too — it works but isn't maintained. oauth scope decides what it can see. grant read-only and a specific folder where you can.
22. gmail
read and send mail.
install: community server via npx, oauth on first call
link: https://github.com/GongRzhe/Gmail-MCP-Server
gotcha: send is a side effect that leaves your account. never let an agent send mail unsupervised. community-maintained — vet it.
23. google calendar
events, scheduling, availability checks.
install: community server via npx, oauth on first call
link: https://github.com/nspady/google-calendar-mcp
gotcha: creating invites notifies real people. confirm before it writes.
24. asana
tasks, projects, workload. official v2 remote server (went GA early 2026).
install: 
 
then complete oauth
link: https://developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-mcp-server
gotcha: don't use the old /sse beta endpoint — it was deprecated and shut down may 2026. inherits your asana permissions.
25. airtable
records, bases, schema.
install: 
 
link: https://github.com/domdomegg/airtable-mcp-server
gotcha: community-maintained, well regarded. scope the pat to specific bases.
 
payments & fintech
26. stripe
payments, subscriptions, refunds, customer lookups. official.
install:
 
link: https://docs.stripe.com/mcp
gotcha: refunds and subscription changes move real money. stripe's own docs recommend enabling human confirmation on tools and warn about prompt-injection when mixing with other servers. control scope with a restricted api key. read-only until proven.
27. paypal
invoices, transactions, payouts via the official paypal agent toolkit / mcp.
install: paypal ships an official remote mcp plus the paypal agent toolkit; follow paypal's developer docs for the current endpoint and oauth setup
link: https://www.paypal.ai
gotcha: same as stripe. money-moving tools stay supervised — confirm every write.
28. plaid
bank data aggregation, balances, transactions.
install: official plaid MCP, oauth flow
link: https://plaid.com/docs/
gotcha: this is people's banking data. read-only, and think hard about where the context window ends up.
29. quickbooks
bookkeeping, invoicing, reconciliation.
install: community/intuit server, oauth
link: https://developer.intuit.com
gotcha: accounting writes have downstream consequences (tax, audit). keep a human signing off.
 
blockchain & web3
heads up for this whole section: these touch real assets on chains where transactions are irreversible. 
the well-built ones never hold your private keys and always make you confirm in a separate wallet UI. that design is the whole point — respect it.
30. base mcp
coinbase's official onchain gateway, launched may 26, 2026. swap tokens, send funds, track a portfolio, hit defi protocols (uniswap, morpho, moonwell, aerodrome, avantis, bankr, virtuals) — all by chatting. 
oAuth 2.1, fully non-custodial: the server never holds your private keys. when the agent requests a transaction it builds the call locally and stores it as a pending request that your base account retrieves for you to review and sign. nothing executes onchain without your approval in the base app.
install: install base mcp inside a supported client (claude, chatgpt, cursor) and authenticate with your base account — base's official docs/blog have the current setup; i'm not quoting an exact endpoint string here because i couldn't verify one to the character, and a wrong url on a money-moving server isn't worth the risk.
link: https://github.com/base/base-mcp
gotcha: the old base-mcp npm package is deprecated — do not npx base-mcp. and understand what you're authorizing: this can move real funds on an irreversible chain. the review-and-sign step in the base app is your safety net. never bypass it.
31. solana agent kit
onchain actions on solana — transfers, swaps, token ops.
install: community server via npx, wallet key in env
link: https://github.com/sendaifun/solana-agent-kit
gotcha: many community solana servers want a hot private key in env. that's a real risk. prefer setups that sign in a separate wallet, and never put a key holding real funds in a config file.
32. thirdweb
deploy and interact with smart contracts across evm chains.
install: thirdweb ships an mcp server; check thirdweb's docs for the current package/command and where to put your secret key
link: https://portal.thirdweb.com
gotcha: contract deploys are irreversible and cost gas. test on a testnet chain id first.
33. the graph
query onchain data via subgraphs without running an indexer.
install: community server via npx
link: https://thegraph.com/docs/
gotcha: read-only by nature, low risk. mostly a data tool.
34. dune
onchain analytics — run and read dune queries from the agent.
install: community server, dune api key in env
link: https://dune.com/docs/api/
gotcha: api credits are metered. a chatty agent can burn through a free tier fast.
35. etherscan
block explorer access — contract verification, tx lookups, abi fetch.

how to actually choose
if you build software: github, context7, playwright, your database (postgres/supabase/neon), sentry. five servers, 90% of the value.
if you ship content: higgsfield, davinci resolve, elevenlabs, youtube, figma. that's a full creator pipeline.
if you trade or work onchain: start read-only — coingecko, polygon, the graph, dune. add base mcp or alpaca only when you understand the confirmation flow cold, and paper-trade first.
if you run a company on docs and tickets: slack, linear/jira, notion, google drive. the agent stops being a chat window and starts being a teammate.
the trap is installing everything because it sounds useful. don't. each connected server eats context and drags performance on the work you actually care about. 
three to five sharp picks beat twenty dull ones every time. revisit the config quarterly — the ecosystem moves fast, and a server you set up before march 2026 has probably been superseded by something faster and better-authed.
pick your five. wire them in. ship.
